An account of two types of what I call ‘heteronomous defeat’ for propositional knowledge is developed and defended: one on which propositional knowledge is defeated when the subject acquires a belief that either indicates the target belief is epistemically heteronymous (i.e. Type 1) or calls into doubt the reliability of the subject’s belief-forming process as one that would (reliably enough) result in an epistemically autonomous belief (i.e. Type 2). Recognizing heteronomous defeat as a genuine form of knowledge defeat fits snugly with the wider idea that knowledge defeaters, as such, are indicators of ignorance.</jats:p>\", \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.1093/oso/9780192846921.003.0003\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2022, 2, 1]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.4324/9781003003465-3\", \"title\": [\"Epistemic Autonomy and Externalism\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.4324/9781003003465-3\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2021, 7, 6]]}}, {\"DOI\": \"10.4324/9781003003465-13\", \"title\": [\"The Virtue of Epistemic Autonomy\"], \"URL\": \"https://doi.org/10.4324/9781003003465-13\", \"published\": {\"date-parts\": [[2021, 7, 6]]}}]", "excerpt_truncated": false, "source_sha256": "bc66caf9f87e7cd17fa588b73687be9f2216281acae3a14c3ebf41ea8fc46688", "verification_required": true, "topic_domain": "obedience_limits", "evidence_role": "discovery", "host_tier": "discovery", "source_identity": null, "persistent_ide…
